title: Yesterday, again
description: More of the past, with the other two verb endings.
grammarNote: The preterite of an -er or -ir verb: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron.

explanation.summary: The -er and -ir verbs share one set of preterite endings, and the pattern is the same as the -ar verbs with the accent moved. The irregular verbs are the ones to watch.

sections.heading: One set of endings
sections.body: Both families take -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. Comer becomes comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron. Vivir becomes viví, viviste, vivió, vivimos, vivisteis, vivieron. Compare with the -ar form, which ends in ó for the third person: habló.

examples.en: You lived in Madrid for two years.

sections.heading: The yo form changes the stem
sections.body: A number of -er and -ir verbs change the stem in the yo form of the preterite, and drop the ending: pedir becomes pedí, venir becomes vine, decir becomes dije, poder became pude, tener became tuve, hacer became hice. And the third person of the very irregular verbs changes too: dijo, hizo, tuvo, vino, pudo.

sections.heading: Choosing between the two pasts
sections.body: Use the preterite for a finished event with a time attached, and the imperfect for how things were. The imperfect is the one you use for the background of a story: de niño jugaba en el parque. The preterite moves the story forward: un día, jugué en el parque.

examples.es: Un día, jugué en el parque.
examples.en: One day, I played in the park.

examples.es: De niño, jugaba en el parque.
examples.en: As a child, I used to play in the park.
When I was small, I did not read.

items.note: The preterite of pedir. The yo form is pedí.
The preterite of entender. The yo form is entendí.
The preterite of llegar. The yo form is llegué.
The preterite of salir. The yo form is salí.
